regions.name: Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm
regions.image: The long lake under the northern moon

events.text: A water cultivator founds Hàm Nguyệt Trang on the long lake, saying the moon in the lake is easier to catch than the one in the sky.
In the Long Lake War, Băng Tâm skiffs raid the pearl beds of Hàm Nguyệt Trang; the manor sinks its own boats rather than lose them.
Kiều Nguyệt Châu becomes mistress of Hàm Nguyệt Trang and doubles the pearl harvest within twenty years.

residents.name: Kiều Nguyệt Châu
residents.role: Mistress of Hàm Nguyệt Trang, water arts, spirit fish and lake pearls

seat_of.name: Hàm Nguyệt Trang
seat_of.craft: water arts; spirit fish and lake pearls
seat_of.note: The long northern lake holds the cold moon of its region, Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm

events.text: Birds return to the lake each autumn in such numbers that the traders' camp on the shore is called Quy Điểu.
Trade in lake pearls makes Quy Điểu Trấn rich; its market is held on the ice every winter.
Reindeer herders settle on the lake's snowy north shore; their camp becomes Tuyết Lộc Thôn.
A winter so cold that smoke freezes above the chimneys gives Hàn Yên Thôn its name.
A snow-leopard spirit beast takes a child from Hàn Yên Thôn; Hàm Nguyệt Trang's disciples track it for forty days across the ice.
Tùng Đào's first steward of the north builds warm stone houses for the lake villages; the hamlet beside them is still called Noãn Ốc.
A hot spring is found under the snow at Noãn Ốc; old cultivators come to soak their bones every winter.

places.name: Hạo Nguyệt Hồ
places.note: The long lake of Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm, the biggest on the continent; Hàm Nguyệt Trang holds its moon

events.text: Fishers on the long lake say that five years ago they saw a man walk over the water into the moon; they build a shrine on the shore.
A fisher of Tuyết Lộc pulls a pearl the size of a fist from Hạo Nguyệt Hồ; Hàm Nguyệt Trang buys it and begins to farm pearls.
Hạo Nguyệt Hồ freezes to its bed for one winter; the spirit fish of Hàm Nguyệt Trang live through it in the moon's reflection.
Tùng Đào Cung and Băng Tâm Các go to war over Hạo Nguyệt Hồ and its pearls.
Đỗ Tinh Hà arbitrates the Long Lake War: the lake stays Tùng Đào's, and Băng Tâm may fish its northern shore.
A white moon-fox is seen on the lake three nights running; the villagers say a blessed land is waking somewhere in the north.

places.name: Phản Cảnh Lâm
places.note: Vương Duy, Lộc Trại: phản cảnh nhập thâm lâm (the evening light comes back into the deep forest); the heart of the northern forest

events.text: The evening light lingers so long in the heart of Phản Cảnh Lâm that lost travellers walk by it until dawn; the forest takes its name.
Hunters find footprints in the snow leading into Phản Cảnh Lâm and never out; no one follows them.

regions.name: Tuyết Hỏa Giác
regions.image: A cold cape with volcanic isles and hot springs

famous_sites.name: Đào Nguyên Cảnh
famous_sites.gloss: Realm of the Peach Blossom Spring
famous_sites.note: Đào Uyên Minh: a fisherman follows a stream of peach petals through a cave into a hidden valley, and can never find it again. Its gate is a cave by a forest stream.

events.text: Alchemists light a furnace with fire carried from the volcanic isles and found Hồng Lô Cốc.
Đồng Hồng Lô becomes master of Hồng Lô Cốc and keeps its furnace burning for nine years without cooling.
The volcanic isles smoke for a month; Hồng Lô Cốc's alchemists sail out to gather the ash before the rain does.

residents.name: Đồng Hồng Lô
residents.role: Head of Hồng Lô Cốc, alchemy over volcanic fire

seat_of.name: Hồng Lô Cốc
seat_of.note: Hồng lô điểm tuyết (a snowflake on a red furnace, gone at once), the cape of snow and fire

places.name: Yên Ba Thành
places.note: Thôi Hiệu, Hoàng Hạc Lâu: yên ba giang thượng sử nhân sầu (mist on the river waves makes one sad); the haze of Thúy Vi

events.text: Thúy Vi Tông founds Yên Ba Thành, a port in the mist of the river waves.
Thúy Vi Tông founds Mục Ca Thành on its cape, where herders sing to their flocks.
Grain prices in Mục Ca Thành double after a poor harvest; the herders sing their songs for coin in Yên Ba's streets.
The Thẩm family, fishers of the white sands, build the first houses of Bạch Sa.
A daughter of the Thẩm clan marries into a merchant house of Yên Ba; the white sands become a trading town.
A fisher of Bạch Sa nets a peach petal in midwinter, far from any peach tree; the elders say the hidden valley's stream has opened again.
Wheat grows in the warm ash of the cape; the first fields of Mạch Lãng Thôn ripple like waves.
The sailors of Phong Phàm Thôn learn to read the cape's winds so well that their sails never go slack.
Grain from Hòa Thử Thôn feeds Yên Ba Thành through the long winter of 860.
A pirate crew hides all winter in the cove below Ẩn Loan Thôn; the villagers feed them and say nothing.
When Thôn Hải falls, the pirates of Ẩn Loan cove vanish in one night, leaving a chest of salt and a child.

places.name: Hỏa Ngọc Mạch
places.note: Under a volcano on an island off Tuyết Hỏa Giác, far out in the western sea, where Lạc Hà's waters begin.

events.text: Thúy Vi's surveyors chart the cape and find a pocket of fire jade far out at sea; they name it Hỏa Ngọc Mạch and keep the chart sealed.

places.name: Hỏa Hồ Nguyên
places.note: Tundra of Tuyết Hỏa Giác, the horn of snow and fire, where fire foxes run on the snow.

places.name: Tuyết Để Tuyền
places.note: Hot water rising under the snowfields of Tuyết Hỏa Giác.

places.name: Hồ Tâm Thang
places.gloss: Hot Water at the Lake's Heart
places.note: Hot springs on an island in the lake of Tuyết Hỏa Giác.

regions.name: Thanh Loan Lĩnh
regions.image: The hills whose haze names Thúy Vi Tông

fallen_sects.name: Không Sơn Viện
fallen_sects.cause: no heir; its master gave the hills to Thúy Vi's founder

events.text: Phùng Yên Hà founds Thúy Vi Tông in the blue-green mist of the north-western hills.
Ngu Lam Sơn, the new head, walks in the haze for a hundred days before giving his first order.
Phùng Yên Hà dies at 640; Ngu Lam Sơn becomes head of Thúy Vi Tông and takes the White Cloud Whisk.

residents.name: Quyền Thanh Lam
residents.role: First elder of Thúy Vi Tông (age 360)

events.text: Tống Tọa Vân, the last student of the empty mountain, founds Vân Khởi Quán, to walk where the water ends and watch the clouds rise.

residents.name: Tống Tọa Vân
residents.role: Abbot of Vân Khởi Quán, a Daoist abbey of mountain hermits and teachers

seat_of.name: Vân Khởi Quán
seat_of.craft: a Daoist abbey of mountain hermits and teachers
seat_of.note: Vương Duy: hành đáo thủy cùng xứ, tọa khán vân khởi thời (walk to where the water ends, sit and watch the clouds rise)

places.name: Hàn Tân Thành
places.note: The northern ford and port of the cold coast

events.text: Under Không Sơn Viện, fishers and ferrymen build Hàn Tân Thành at the cold ford of the north coast.
Tùng Đào Cung marches on the Cold Ford coast of Thúy Vi Tông without asking the Pivot for a writ.
Tùng Đào takes the Cold Ford coast and Hàn Tân Thành; Chung Hoài Cực, Kỳ Tùng Ẩn's old drinking friend, lets it stand, and the Compact's first crack shows.
Under Tùng Đào's rule the fishers of the Cold Ford are taxed in pine resin they do not have; many leave for the hills.
Thúy Vi Tông, holding the Pivot's writ, marches to take back the Cold Ford.
Thúy Vi retakes the Cold Ford coast and Hàn Tân Thành after 233 years.
When the Cold Ford comes home, the fishers of Hàn Tân light lamps on every boat for a month.

places.name: Lam Yên Thị
places.note: Below Thúy Vi Tông's seat, in the haze that names it

events.text: A market grows at the foot of Thúy Vi Tông in the mountain mist; it is called Lam Yên Thị.
Không Sơn's students plant the cypress groves around Bách Diệp as a lesson in patience.
Woodcutters singing on the ridges below Không Sơn Viện are asked to sing more quietly; the town they found is still called Tiều Ca.
Crows gather on the ridge in such numbers that the village beneath is named Ô Đề.
A spring in the woods above Lâm Tuyền Thôn cures the coughing sickness of 760; the village is named for its woods and springs.
Red leaves from Thu Diệp Thôn are sold in Lam Yên Thị as bookmarks for scripture; scholars come from three sects to buy them.

places.name: Bích Ngọc Khoáng
places.note: Green stone from the green hills of Thúy Vi.

events.text: Green jade is found in the hills; Không Sơn Viện forbids mining it, so the mountain stays quiet.
With the hills now Thúy Vi's, the green jade mine of Bích Ngọc Khoáng is opened at last.

places.name: Vân Mẫu Khoáng
places.note: Mica, 'mother of clouds', for Vân Khởi Quán, the abbey of rising clouds.

events.text: The monks of Vân Khởi Quán open the mica mine and say the stone is cloud made solid.
The mica of Vân Mẫu Khoáng runs thin; the abbot Tống Tọa Vân says that clouds, too, pass.

places.name: Không Sơn Viện
places.note: Left empty after its master gave the hills to Thúy Vi's founder; quiet and never looted.

events.text: Bùi Lộc Trại founds Không Sơn Viện in the hills of Thanh Loan Lĩnh, an academy so quiet that, as the poem says, on the empty mountain no one is seen.
Bùi Lộc Trại dies; Thôi Bất Kiến becomes the master of Không Sơn Viện, and takes no disciple but one boy, Tống Tọa Vân.
Thôi Bất Kiến, with no heir, gives Thanh Loan Lĩnh, his whisk and his only student to Phùng Yên Hà; the empty mountain becomes Thúy Vi's.
Thôi Bất Kiến dies in the empty academy he gave away; Phùng Yên Hà leaves it as it was, unlocked and unlooted.
A landslide on the ridge uncovers a stone gate carved with Không Sơn's poem; Thúy Vi seals it again.
A traveller who spends a night in the empty Không Sơn Viện swears he heard someone reading aloud in the next room.

places.name: Băng Tê Nguyên
places.note: Tundra of Thanh Loan Lĩnh crossed by ice rhinoceroses.

regions.name: Thâm Tùng Hải
regions.image: Pine forest as wide as a sea

events.text: Kỳ Tùng Ẩn founds Tùng Đào Cung among the endless pines, with his first disciple Thôi Khinh Hồng, then 120.
Kỳ Tùng Ẩn dies at 620; his first disciple Thôi Khinh Hồng becomes the second head of Tùng Đào Cung.
Thôi Khinh Hồng, the second head of Tùng Đào Cung, retires at 820 to the retreat by its seat, and her disciple Đàm Tùng Lại, then 380, takes the headship.

residents.name: Thôi Khinh Hồng
residents.role: Disciple of the founder Kỳ Tùng Ẩn (age 1,120). Second head of Tùng Đào Cung, retired in year 900 to the retreat by its seat; the sect's one Hóa Thần

residents.name: Hồ Tùng Nguyệt
residents.role: First elder of Tùng Đào Cung (age 400)

events.text: A monk plays the zither in the pines of Thâm Tùng Hải until it sounds like ten thousand ravines; his listeners found Vạn Hác Viện and keep the Tùng Phong Cầm.
A Vạn Hác student plays so well under the pines that Thiên Xu's envoy forgets his message.

residents.name: Hà Thính Tùng
residents.role: Head of Vạn Hác Viện, the zither and sound cultivation

seat_of.name: Vạn Hác Viện
seat_of.gloss: Academy of the Ten Thousand Ravines
seat_of.craft: sound cultivation: the zither (cầm) and its arts
seat_of.note: Lý Bạch, on hearing a monk play the zither: như thính vạn hác tùng (like pines in ten thousand ravines), the pine waves of its lord

places.name: Tùng Gian Thành
places.note: Vương Duy: minh nguyệt tùng gian chiếu (the bright moon shines among the pines)

events.text: Tùng Đào Cung raises Tùng Gian Thành among the pines below its palace.
Tùng Gian Thành holds its first Night of a Thousand Pines, hanging a lantern on every tree around the city.

places.name: Tùng Hạ Thị
places.note: Giả Đảo: tùng hạ vấn đồng tử (beneath the pine I asked the boy where his master was)

events.text: Pilgrims who come to hear the pine waves of the new palace stay on; Tùng Hạ Thị begins as a ring of tents beneath the pines.
Lâm Dã Hạc is born in Tùng Hạ Thị to a woodcutter's family; a crane lands on the roof the day he is born.
Wolves from the deep pines follow the caravans to Tùng Hạ Thị; Tùng Đào doubles the road watch.

residents.name: Lâm Dã Hạc
residents.role: A loose cultivator, a rising talent with no sect (age 55)

events.text: A deer calls at the forest's edge every dawn for a year; the Lâm family settles where it called and names the place Lộc Minh.
The Lâm clan's woodcarvers of Lộc Minh make the beams of a new hall in Tùng Gian Thành from a single fallen pine.
Tùng Đào Cung founds Cổ Độ Thành at the old ferry on its southern river.
In the War of the Pivot, the ferrymen of Cổ Độ carry the iron chain for Thiết Tỏa Quan link by link.
Iron links from the chain of Thiết Tỏa Quan are dragged from the river at Cổ Độ; smiths pay well for them.
White birches grow where a forest fire burned; the new village is named Bạch Hoa.
The survivors of Hổ Khiếu move to Thanh Tùng Thôn and plant a green pine for each of their dead.
Vạn Hác Viện's zither students practise in Tùng Phong hamlet; the villagers learn to sleep through anything.

places.name: Thạch Lục Khoáng
places.note: Malachite, the green of the pine sea, dug under the trees.

events.text: Malachite is found under the roots of the oldest pines; Tùng Đào lets it be dug only where no tree must be cut.

places.name: Thương Tùng Mạch
places.note: A wild vein under the old pine sea, 4 tiles from Thiên Xu's border.

events.text: Tùng Đào fences the grey pines over an old spirit vein near the heart; it is called Thương Tùng Mạch.

places.name: Hổ Khiếu Trấn
places.note: A forest town overrun by a beast tide.

events.text: Woodsmen found Hổ Khiếu Trấn deep in the pine sea, where the tigers are.
A tiger as large as a house is seen near Hổ Khiếu Trấn; Tùng Đào sends three disciples, and two come back.
A beast tide pours out of the deep pines and overruns Hổ Khiếu Trấn; the tigers' roar is the last thing its people hear.

places.name: Thiết Tỏa Quan
places.note: Lưu Vũ Tích: the thousand-fathom iron chain sank to the river bed. The Tùng Đào and Lạc Hà fort that Thiên Xu broke in the War of the Pivot.

events.text: The allies raise Thiết Tỏa Quan and stretch an iron chain across the river road to the heart.
Thiên Xu Tông breaks Thiết Tỏa Quan; the thousand-fathom chain sinks to the river bed.
